packs.name: Budget Tracker
packs.summary: A finance dashboard: one-click capture, live balances, budgets with rings, this month at a glance — from one ledger.
packs.description: Five small databases that stay filled in, and a dashboard that reads them. `budget` is the ledger: one row per transaction with a date, an amount, a kind (expense, income, transfer), a category and the account it hit — a transfer names both accounts. Its page is the dashboard: New expense / New income / New transfer buttons, this month's spent, earned and net as tiles, the budgets as cards with a ring each, spending grouped by month with totals, a donut of where the money went, and every account's balance. `accounts` holds one row per account with its opening balance; income, spending, transfers in and out and the balance are computed from the ledger. `budget-limits` holds one row per category with the monthly amount you mean to spend and shows spent, remaining and the share used as a ring. `budget-bills` is every recurring charge with its cycle and next due date: tick paid and the date moves forward one cycle in the same row. `budget-wishlist` is what you are saving up for: tag a transfer with `wish` and the item shows how much is put by and how much is left, tag the purchase and it moves to Bought at what it really cost. Everything is computed from the rows when you open the page; nothing is copied between databases and nothing needs resetting on the 1st.
packs.credits: The dashboard shape — quick-action buttons, budget rings, month-grouped lists, a donut and account balances — follows Sentele's Finance Tracker and Notion's Personal Finance Tracker; the single ledger with transfers as rows and everything computed on read is our own.

packs.name: Contacts
packs.summary: People with a keep-in-touch cadence and a log of every conversation: who is overdue, follow-ups, history.
packs.description: A personal CRM in two databases. Contacts is one row per person: how you know them, how often you mean to be in touch (monthly, quarterly, twice a year…), plus company, role, birthday, and a page for how you met and what to remember. Interactions is one row per conversation — date, who, what kind, one line of summary — and every person's page embeds their own history from it. The person's `last_seen` is read from their newest interaction, `quiet_days` counts from it, and `due_in` measures that against the cadence, so the Reach out view is the people who are actually overdue, most overdue first, with nothing to update by hand. Follow-ups due lists the promises whose date has come, the Follow-ups calendar shows the ones ahead, and the month chart, one bar per kind, shows whether you are keeping in touch.
packs.credits: The keep-in-touch cadence comes from Dex and the tiered personal CRMs in Notion's gallery (Circles of Trust); the one-file-per-interaction log and the person page that lists its own meetings come from Dann Berg's Obsidian people template and the obsidian-personal-crm plugin.

packs.name: Content Calendar
packs.summary: Content from idea to published: pipeline board, calendar, this week, overdue, a queue with days left, campaigns, chart.
packs.description: One row per piece of content — the row is the draft. `status` carries it from idea through drafting, review and scheduled to published; `channel` and `format` say where and what; `due` is the draft deadline and `publish` the day it goes out, with `days_left` counted down for you and `published_on` stamped when it ships. The Pipeline board is the flow, the Calendar is the month, This week is Monday to Sunday, Overdue is every draft past its deadline, the Queue is what is next in publish order, Ideas is the inbox with the high priority ones on top, and a bar chart counts what shipped per month, one bar per channel. A newsletter or episode with `repeat: weekly` comes back on its own once published. Campaigns are a second collection: a launch or a series with a start and an end on a timeline, counting its pieces and how many have shipped, with its own page that shows them as a live board and schedule. Each piece's page carries a brief, an outline, the draft, a publish checklist and a table of what was repurposed from it.
packs.credits: Shaped by the content and editorial calendars in Notion's gallery (Notion's own Content Calendar and Social Media Calendar, Easlo's Content Calendar, Thomas Frank's Creator's Companion) and by Bases-driven calendars in the Obsidian community.

packs.name: Daily Note
packs.summary: One page per day with mood, energy and sleep: this week's days, a calendar of the days you wrote, weekly trend charts.
packs.description: A journal as a database: every day is one row with a `mood`, an `energy` (stars out of five) and `sleep` (hours), the areas it touched and a one-line highlight, plus a page whose body is the day — an intention and three priorities in the morning, a timestamped log as you go, a short evening reflection. This week lists the days since Monday in order, ready to read before a weekly review; the calendar shows the days you wrote (and the gaps); the Energy and Sleep charts average each week so a bad month is visible before you feel it; the Moods chart stacks each month's days by mood. New row gives you today in one keystroke, already titled with the date and linked to its week. Pairs with Weekly Review (which counts and averages the week's days from here) and Habit Tracker (habits stay in their own log).
packs.credits: Mood, energy and sleep as properties with a calendar and weekly trend charts is the shape of the best-rated daily journals in Notion's gallery (Eve Jiyū's Daily Reflection Journal, mrpugo's Energy Journal, Easlo's minimal journal); the morning-intention / log / evening-highlight body follows the Obsidian daily-note templates of Sébastien Dubois and Vault of Josh.

packs.name: Decision Log
packs.summary: One row per decision: context, options, what was chosen and why, a review date that comes due by itself, the outcome.
packs.description: A decisions database rather than a loose note. Each row carries `status` (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded), an `area`, its `impact` and whether it is `reversible`, your `confidence` at the time and, once you have looked back, the `outcome`. The dates take care of themselves: `decided` is stamped the day a row is accepted, `reviewed` the day you set an outcome, and `days_to_review` counts down to the `review` date you chose. The row's page is the record: context and state of mind, the options with their good and bad points, the decision and the one reason that carried it, what you expect to happen, the consequences, and a review section you fill in on the review date. A `supersedes` relation links a new decision to the one it replaces, and the old row's `superseded_by` fills in on its own. Views: Log, Board by status, Due for review (the next thirty days and anything overdue), a Timeline from decided to review, Outcomes by month and a Calibration chart of outcomes by the confidence you wrote down. Works for a team's architecture decisions and for one person's life ones.
packs.credits: Architecture decision records (Michael Nygard; the MADR template), Farnam Street's decision journal, and the decision databases in Notion's gallery that add a review date and an outcome.

packs.name: Goals
packs.summary: Goals with milestones and dated check-ins; progress and days left computed per goal, a weekly review list, a timeline.
packs.description: Three databases. `goals` is one row per goal with its life area, timeframe (year, quarter, month), priority, start and target dates, a one-line measure of done, and a status that says planned, on track, at risk, off track, done or dropped; its progress bar, last check-in date, share of milestones done, next milestone date and days left are computed from the other two databases every time you look, and the day you mark it done is stamped for you. `goal-milestones` breaks a goal into dated steps with a status board, an overdue list and a calendar. `goal-checkins` is the review log: one short row per check-in with the date, the progress number and your confidence, so progress is a line over time instead of a number you overwrite. Due for review lists the open goals with no check-in in a week; the Timeline lays them out from start to target. Open a goal and its page lists its milestones, charts its check-ins and keeps the why, the plan and the obstacles under them.
packs.credits: Goals / milestones / check-ins follows the goal trackers in Notion's gallery (Benny Builds It, Jithin Rajiv, Easlo, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Brain) and the OKR check-in habit; the per-goal progress chart and the computed-on-read columns are our own.

packs.name: Habit Tracker
packs.summary: Habits as rows, one file per day; streaks, day scores and a year heatmap computed on read, never stored.
packs.description: Each habit is a row with its own page; each day is one small file whose `done:` list names what you did. Tick today in the Today view (Space on a habit, or `mod+shift+h` for "Log today…" from anywhere), and the week grid, month, and year heatmap fill in on their own — current and longest streaks, perfect days, completion — all computed from the files, so nothing is ever reset and nothing goes stale. A day with no file is a day with nothing done; the first tick creates it. Pair it with `templates/daily-with-habits.md` as your daily note so today's habits sit at the top of your journal.
packs.credits: The streak, heatmap and week-grid ideas come from the habit trackers in Notion's gallery; the day-file model is our own so history is never reset.

packs.name: Meeting Notes
packs.summary: Meetings as rows with date, kind, status and attendees; action items in their own list, linked to the meeting.
packs.description: One row per meeting in `collections/meetings/`: when, what kind, who was there, a one-line summary, a status that moves from scheduled to held to followed-up, and an optional `repeat` that brings a standing meeting back on its own. Open a meeting and the page has the shape a note needs a month later — agenda, notes, decisions, action items, open questions — with a live table of that meeting's action items at the bottom. Action items are rows of their own in `collections/action-items/` with an owner, a due date and a status; the engine counts each meeting's open items and its share closed, stamps `completed` when an item is done, and shows the days left on each. Views: All, This week, Upcoming, To write up, Calendar, a board by status for follow-up, and a chart of meetings per week by kind; on the action items, Open, Overdue, This week, Mine, Board, Due and By week.
packs.credits: The properties and views follow the most-used meeting-notes databases in Notion's gallery and Dann Berg's meeting template for Obsidian; the separate action-items list is the advice that comes up in every review of them.

packs.name: 1:1 Notes
packs.summary: A page per person with a running agenda, one row per 1:1, and the follow-ups from all of them in one list.
packs.description: Three small databases that fit together. `collections/people/` is one page per person you meet regularly: role, cadence, current focus, a topics list that carries from one meeting to the next, and live tables of their 1:1s and open follow-ups. The engine adds the numbers you would otherwise look up — when you last met, the next 1:1 on the books, how many you have held in ninety days, how many promises are open — and a `due` flag that compares the gap since you last met with the person's cadence, so Due is the list to book from and Weekly is a tracker of the weekly people against the 1:1s list. `collections/one-on-ones/` is one row per meeting — date, person, mood, one-line summary, an optional `repeat` that brings a standing 1:1 back when it is held — with a page shaped for the conversation: their topics, yours, since last time, wins, blockers, growth, feedback, follow-ups. `collections/follow-ups/` holds what each of you promised, with an owner, a due date, the days left and a stamped `completed` date, so what you owe, what you are owed and what is overdue are views rather than a search. Charts on the 1:1s page count meetings per week by mood and per month by person.
packs.credits: Sections follow Notion's own one-on-one template (past week, this week, blockers, action items) and Dann Berg's people-note pattern for Obsidian; the person page as the durable record with per-meeting notes underneath is the shape every manager's guide converges on.

packs.name: PARA Index
packs.summary: Projects, Areas and Resources as three linked databases; archive is a status, and an index note shows it all live.
packs.description: The PARA method as databases instead of folders. Areas are the ongoing responsibilities (Health, Finances, Career) with a standard to keep and a review date — a Due for review list shows which have come round, and each area counts its own open projects and resources. Projects have an outcome, a deadline and the area they serve; `start` and `completed` stamp themselves when a project goes active and done, `days_left` counts down, and a Due soon list and a Timeline show where the deadlines pile up. Resources are the articles, books and tools you keep, tied to the area or project they are for, with an inbox that shows how long each has waited. Nothing is ever moved to an Archive folder — a project is `done` or `dropped`, an area or resource is `archived`, and the Archive views filter on that, so relations and history survive. The `Second Brain` note template is the one-page index: active projects, what is due, areas, recent resources and the archive, all live.
packs.credits: The PARA method by Tiago Forte (Building a Second Brain). Archive-as-a-status and the area page that lists its own projects and resources come from the PARA templates in Notion's gallery, notably Thomas Frank's and Notion Mastery's.

packs.name: Project Tracker
packs.summary: Projects with status, priority, deadline, computed progress and one next action; milestones; a timeline; a page each.
packs.description: One row per project, and a second small collection of milestones — the dated steps a project is made of. A project has a status (planned / active / on_hold / done / dropped), a priority, an `area`, `start` and `deadline` dates and one `next_action` so a stalled project is obvious. The rest is computed: `progress` is the share of its milestones ticked done, `next_milestone` the soonest still open, `days_left` a countdown to the deadline, `open_tasks` a count from the Tasks pack when it is installed, and `completed` is stamped the day status becomes done. Views: Open (what is live, p1 first), Board by status, a Timeline from start to deadline, Due in 30 days, Stalled (active projects with no next action) and Finished per month. Each project's page states the outcome, embeds its own milestones, and — if the Tasks pack is installed — a board of the tasks that name it. Milestones have their own calendar, so every key date across every project is on one page.
packs.credits: Follows the project databases in Notion's gallery (Notion's Projects & Tasks, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Brain projects, Easlo's Project Tracker); the single next action is from Getting Things Done.

packs.name: Reading List
packs.summary: Books, articles and papers as rows with a note each, a progress bar per book, and an optional log of sittings.
packs.description: One row per thing you read — book, ebook, audiobook, article or paper — with author, status, format, genre, a star rating, page count, who recommended it and when you started and finished. `started` and `finished` stamp themselves when `status` moves; a `progress` bar is worked out from the pages you have read over the page count. The row's page is the reading note: why you picked it up, the ideas, the quotes, the verdict. A second collection, `reading-log`, holds one small row per sitting (date, book, pages); from those each book sums its `logged` pages and knows its `last_read` day, the Reading list draws a week grid of what you are reading, each book's page a year heatmap, and the log charts pages per week by book. Views: Reading now (with progress and days idle), Shelf by status, Finished (with days to finish), Per month, a Timeline of every book started and This week. The log is optional — the list works without it.
packs.credits: Shaped by the reading trackers in Notion's gallery (Thomas Frank's Books, the Bookworm and Book Tracker templates) and by the Obsidian book-tracking write-ups that keep a list of read dates per book.

packs.name: Recipe Box
packs.summary: Recipes with cook counts and last-cooked dates, a meal plan for today and this week, a grocery list in aisle order.
packs.description: Three collections that work as one kitchen. Recipes carry course, cuisine, main ingredient, diet, difficulty, prep and cook minutes, servings, a star rating, status and source; total minutes, how often and when the recipe was last cooked, when it is next planned and how many of its grocery items are still to buy are worked out from the other two collections, so Quick dinners, Rotation and To try answer themselves. The ingredients are a checklist and the method a numbered list in the body, and the page ends with a live cook log. Meals are one row per planned meal — a date, a slot, a recipe — with a calendar, a Today list, a This week list and board, and a bar chart of what you cooked per week. Groceries are items with an aisle and a `bought` box: the To buy table is the shopping list in aisle order, the board is the shop.
packs.credits: The recipe, meal-plan and grocery trio follows the recipe managers in Notion's gallery (Matthias Frank's meal planner, the Ultimate Home Chef dashboard, the Frugal and Thriving recipe database) and the Recipe Box and Recipe View plugins for Obsidian.

packs.name: Tasks
packs.summary: One row per task with status, priority, due and repeat; Today, This week, Upcoming, Inbox, a board and a done chart.
packs.description: The task list most people end up building, done once. Each task is a row with a status (todo / doing / waiting / someday / done), a priority (p1–p3), a `due` date, an optional `repeat`, an `area` and a free-text `project`. The views are the ones to-do apps ship, and they follow the calendar by themselves: Today (due today or earlier), This week, Upcoming, Inbox for what you captured and have not dated, a board by status, and a chart of tasks finished per week. `completed` is stamped when a task is set to done; a task with `repeat: weekly` comes back with its date moved forward. Each task's page has a "done when" line, a checklist of steps and room for notes. Name the same project in the Project Tracker pack and its page shows these tasks and counts the open ones.
packs.credits: Properties and views follow the task databases in Notion's gallery (Notion's Projects & Tasks, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Tasks, Easlo's Task Tracker) and the due, done and recurrence fields of the Obsidian Tasks plugin.

packs.name: Weekly Review
packs.summary: One row per week: a plan, then the get-clear / get-current review; reviews due, rating and carry-over charted.
packs.description: A weekly review as a database. Each week is a row with a `status` (planned, reviewed, skipped), a `rating` out of ten, a one-line `focus`, the `areas` it touched, a `carried_over` count of what slipped, and a `reviewed_on` date that stamps itself when you mark the week reviewed. The page has two halves: a plan (focus and Top 3) and a review — the Getting Things Done checklist (get clear, get current), then wins, what slipped, lessons, what gave and drained energy, the carried-over list, and next week's three. To review lists every planned week whose Friday has come; a board shows the weeks by status, a calendar puts each on its Monday, and two charts plot the rating and the carry-over count week by week, so a slow decline or a growing backlog is visible. With Daily Note installed, each week also counts the days you wrote and averages their energy and sleep — computed, not copied.
packs.credits: The get-clear / get-current / get-creative checklist is David Allen's Weekly Review from Getting Things Done. Weeks as rated rows with monthly trends follows the weekly review databases in Notion's gallery (Thomas Cerulis, Sharky Progress, Simone Smerilli); the plan-then-review page with a carried-over list is the shape of the Vaultorial and Pensio weekly notes for Obsidian; the wins / slipped / energy prompts follow Michelle Mac's.
